questions.question: In the context of Aromatic Substitution Reactions, what is the major organic product when Benzene reacts under the following conditions: CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl / AlCl₃ catalyst?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Primary propyl carbocation complex undergoes a rapid 1,2-hydride shift to form the more stable isopropyl cation electrophile. The correct major product is 'Cumene [Isopropylbenzene, (CH₃)₂CHPh] (Major)'.

questions.question: In the context of Aromatic Substitution Reactions, what is the major organic product when Benzene reacts under the following conditions: CH₃CH₂COCl / AlCl₃, then H₂O?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: The resonance-stabilized acylium ion (CH₃CH₂-C≡O⁺) electrophile resists rearrangements and prevents polyalkylation. The correct major product is 'Propiophenone [PhCOCH₂CH₃] + HCl'.

questions.question: In the context of Aromatic Substitution Reactions, what is the major organic product when Propiophenone (PhCOCH₂CH₃) reacts under the following conditions: Zn(Hg) / conc. HCl, reflux?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Reduces aryl ketones completely to alkylbenzenes without carbocation rearrangements. The correct major product is 'Propylbenzene (PhCH₂CH₂CH₃)'.

questions.question: In the context of Aromatic Substitution Reactions, what is the major organic product when Acetophenone (PhCOCH₃) reacts under the following conditions: NH₂NH₂, KOH, Diethylene glycol, 200°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Basic reduction of carbonyls via hydrazone intermediates, useful for acid-sensitive substrates. The correct major product is 'Ethylbenzene (PhCH₂CH₃) + N₂(g)'.

questions.question: In the context of Aromatic Substitution Reactions, what is the major organic product when Toluene (PhCH₃) reacts under the following conditions: HNO₃ / H₂SO₄ at 30°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Electron-donating methyl group stabilizes the arenium ion by hyperconjugation preferentially at ortho and para positions. The correct major product is 'o-Nitrotoluene + p-Nitrotoluene (Major mixture)'.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert Nitrobenzene (PhNO₂) into m-Bromonitrobenzene (Major, >90%) in Aromatic Substitution Reactions?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'Nitrobenzene (PhNO₂)' → 'm-Bromonitrobenzene (Major, >90%)' specifically requires 'Br₂ / FeBr₃ at 80°C'. Mechanistic basis: Strongly electron-withdrawing nitro group deactivates all positions but destabilizes the meta arenium ion least.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert Chlorobenzene into o-Chloronitrobenzene + p-Chloronitrobenzene in Aromatic Substitution Reactions?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'Chlorobenzene' → 'o-Chloronitrobenzene + p-Chloronitrobenzene' specifically requires 'HNO₃ / H₂SO₄ at 50°C'. Mechanistic basis: Halogens are deactivating due to electronegativity (induction) but ortho/para directing due to lone pair resonance delocalization.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert 1-Chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene into 1-Methoxy-2,4-dinitrobenzene (2,4-Dinitroanisole) + NaCl in Aromatic Substitution Reactions?
